raw.title: Associate Director, Product Safety & Compliance
raw.excerpt: The OpportunityCaraway Home is looking for an experienced Associate Director, Product Safety & Compliance to build our product compliance function from the ground up and own what we call the Caraway Promise, a testing-obsessed, transparency-first approach to product safety that sets the bar for the industry.
raw.description:
The Opportunity

Caraway Home is looking for an experienced Associate Director, Product Safety & Compliance to build our product compliance function from the ground up and own what we call the Caraway Promise, a testing-obsessed, transparency-first approach to product safety that sets the bar for the industry. The Caraway Promise exists because we believe in transparency, not because the industry requires transparency.

This is a foundational role, the first dedicated compliance hire at Caraway, responsible for building the frameworks, lab relationships, testing strategy, supply chain diligence, claims substantiation, and regulatory sequencing across a diverse and growing product portfolio.You will own the full compliance lifecycle across Caraway's product categories (cookware, bakeware, electrical items, food contact materials, textiles, and packaging), always meeting or exceeding the most stringent applicable global standard to establish industry-leading Caraway protocols and procedures. You will be US-based, work closely with Asia-based suppliers and third-party labs (particularly in China), and build the internal systems and processes that let Caraway scale compliantly, credibly, and with confidence.

Additionally, an important responsibility of this role is disseminating key information, labels, and results to support marketing initiatives. You need to be a strong communicator, working collaboratively with cross functional teams, to broadcast and showcase the diligence Caraway is taking across its entire product portfolio in regards to compliance, being able to assist with crafting accurate, transparent, educational and understandable language and messaging that resonates with our consumer.

This position reports to our Director, Product Development.

Who You Are

You have ten or more years of product safety and regulatory compliance experience in consumer goods, ideally grounded in chemistry, materials science, or applied laboratory research, with deep expertise in food contact materials, cookware, kitchen appliances, or an adjacent hard goods category. You know FDA, LFGB, EU Framework Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004, REACH, CA Prop 65, CA AB 1200, NSF, FSC, and CPSC requirements not as acronyms on a checklist, but as frameworks you've navigated hands-on, including where global standards diverge. You’ll use this fluency to scale the Caraway Promise internationally: building a testing and compliance framework that anticipates global standards.

You are a builder and a scientist at heart, ready to own a compliance program entirely: selecting labs, building testing matrices, writing material certification requirements, establishing supplier audit cadences, and designing the studies needed to substantiate product claims. You operate comfortably across cultures and time zones, with direct experience working with labs and manufacturers in Asia, particularly China. You communicate complex science and regulatory requirements clearly to internal teams (Product, Marketing, Legal, Supply Chain) and external partners alike, and you see internal education as core to the job.

Responsibilities

  • Own and pioneer the Caraway Promise: define and champion a testing-obsessed, transparency-first approach to product safety that goes beyond what regulation requires, because we believe our customers deserve it.
  • Build Caraway's product safety and compliance program, defining frameworks, documentation standards, testing protocols, regulatory calendars, and governance processes across all product categories (cookware, bakeware, small appliances, food contact materials, textiles, and packaging); integrate compliance across the full product lifecycle, from development and supplier onboarding through market placement, ongoing monitoring, and end-of-life.
  • Own and continuously monitor regulatory compliance across US federal and state requirements (FDA food contact, CPSC, CA Prop 65, CA AB 1200, Colorado PFAS Act, and emerging state chemical legislation) and international standards (EU LFGB, EC No 1935/2004, REACH, RoHS, UK REACH post-Brexit), always applying the most stringent applicable standard; lead regulatory change management as a distinct workstream, assessing impact and briefing stakeholders ahead of deadlines.
  • Lead product component mapping and material disclosure, maintaining a complete picture of every material, coating, pigment, and component across Caraway's supply chain, including Declarations of Compliance, material safety data sheets, and test reports.
  • Design and manage Caraway's testing strategy, selecting and managing third-party labs (particularly in Asia, including NRTLs for small appliances), defining testing scope and frequency by product type and risk level, and sequencing testing within development timelines to avoid launch delays or costly late-stage findings.
  • Own claims substantiation: design and commission the clinical, laboratory, and comparative studies (for example migration testing, coating durability, comparative non-stick performance) needed to support our non-toxic, food-safe, and sustainability claims. Partner with Marketing and Customer Research on which claims to make and how to communicate them, and ensure all claims are legally defensible and compliant with FTC guidelines and retailer requirements (Target, Crate & Barrel, Bloomingdale's, etc.), including CA AB 1200 disclosure obligations.
  • Conduct supply chain compliance diligence, including BSCI and Sedex (SMETA) social compliance audits and material certifications (OEKO-TEX, FSC, GRS, GOTS); embed Caraway's material and safety standards directly into manufacturing quality plans in China so factory teams implement them consistently on the production line, not just on paper; manage supplier CAPA processes and produce performance reporting to inform sourcing decisions.
  • Serve as Caraway's internal subject matter expert on product safety and science, building internal education that embeds our standards into onboarding and cross-functional fluency by year one; act as the primary point of contact for retailers, certifying bodies, and regulatory agencies on compliance matters.
  • Own product incident management, leading investigations into consumer complaints and non-conformances, conducting root cause analysis, implementing CAPAs, and coordinating with Legal, Customer Experience, and Operations on any product withdrawal or CPSC recall process; maintaining documentation and reporting readiness for regulatory inquiries.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • 10+ years of product safety, regulatory compliance, or quality assurance experience in consumer goods, with at least 5 years focused on food contact materials, cookware, kitchen appliances, or closely adjacent hard-goods categories; demonstrated ownership across the full compliance lifecycle, from concept and supplier qualification through launch and incident response. No junior or generalist profiles.
  • Deep, working knowledge of food contact material regulations including FDA 21 CFR, LFGB (Chapters 30/31), EU Framework Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004, REACH, CA Prop 65, CA AB 1200, FSC, NSF, and the Colorado PFAS Chemicals Consumer Protection Act; familiarity with UK REACH and other international frameworks is a strong plus.
  • Background in chemistry, materials science, or applied laboratory and clinical research, with direct experience designing and running studies used to substantiate product safety or performance claims.
  • Demonstrated experience managing third-party lab relationships in Asia (China in particular), including test plan scoping, report interpretation, and navigating discrepancies between lab results and supplier-provided data.
  • Hands-on experience with social compliance and supply chain auditing programs, including BSCI and Sedex/SMETA (2- and 4-pillar); familiarity with material certification schemes (OEKO-TEX Standard 100, FSC, GRS, GOTS); skilled at managing CAPA processes and building supplier performance scorecards.
  • Proven ability to develop and manage product testing strategies, including migration testing, heavy metals (lead, cadmium), PFAS/PFOA screening, sensory evaluation, and applicable electrical safety standards (UL, ETL, IEC 60335) for small appliances.
  • Familiarity with FTC Green Guides and CPSC Section 15(b) reporting obligations, product recall mechanics, and the CPSC Fast Track Recall Program.
  • Ability to build and maintain product component maps and material traceability documentation across a multi-supplier, multi-category portfolio, including Declarations of Compliance, mill certificates, glaze and coating specifications, and batch-level test records.
  • Strong cross-functional communication and risk management skills; able to translate scientific and regulatory findings into clear, prioritized guidance for Product, Marketing, Legal, Sourcing, and Supply Chain, and to present compliance risk and status to senior leadership.
  • Demonstrated experience building compliance programs or functions in an environment with limited existing infrastructure; entrepreneurial by nature, with the ability to prioritize and execute without relying on inherited playbooks.
  • Ability to travel internationally to visit manufacturing partners and labs in Asia, up to 35 to 40% annually; experience working with facilities in China required, with additional familiarity across Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia) a plus.
  • Proficiency in Mandarin (spoken and/or written) is a bonus; at minimum, demonstrated effectiveness working through translation with Mandarin-speaking suppliers, factories, and lab contacts.
  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Food Science, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related field, with hands-on laboratory or clinical research experience a strong plus; advanced degree or professional certification (for example RAPS, ISO Lead Auditor) a plus.
  • Experience with small appliance safety standards (UL 60335-1, IEC 60335-2 series, ETL) preferred; experience managing certification processes with Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratories (NRTLs) a plus.
  • Familiarity with retailer compliance and vendor onboarding requirements (Target, Crate & Barrel, Bloomingdale's, Costco, Amazon) and the documentation standards they require from suppliers.

Please note that the duties and responsibilities outlined in this job description are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by employees assigned to this position. It is not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required for the role. Additional tasks and responsibilities may be assigned as needed to meet business needs.

The anticipated base salary range for this role is $140,000 to $160,000. Final compensation will depend on a variety of factors determining base pay at offer, including but not limited to skills, qualifications, and experience. This range provides the opportunity to progress as you grow and develop within the role.

Who We Are

Caraway is a home goods brand on a mission to craft well-designed, non-toxic essentials that thoughtfully raise the standards of what you cook with. We're passionate about creating elevated products, made without forever chemicals, that are better for you, your family, and the planet. We prioritize a holistic approach to the creation of Caraway products. We partner with ethical manufacturers where their employees are safe, paid fairly, given benefits, and work regulated hours. Our eco-friendly manufacturing process emits less CO2 than traditional non-stick coatings, and we use sustainable packaging practices and ship in packaging made from recycled materials. We pride ourselves on continuously striving to do and be better, for you and the planet, in every step of the process.

Since launching in November 2019, we've become one of the fastest growing digitally native brands of the last decade and are now sold in retailers including Target, Bloomingdale's, Crate & Barrel, The Container Store, Costco, Zola, and many more.

We've amassed over 200,000+ five-star reviews from more than 2.5M+ happy customers and thousands of press hits from the likes of Vogue, Domino, Good Housekeeping, Food & Wine, Architectural Digest, PureWow, Fortune, and CNN.

Caraway is a fully remote company filled with motivated and hardworking innovators and doers. We're continually developing programs to support our distributed team to ensure a successful remote experience. If you're looking to join a brand that folks love, read on and apply!

Life at Caraway

raw.description:
More than one million people in the United States today are fighting blood cancer. While a traditional allogeneic stem cell transplant has been the best hope for many, the transplant itself can prove fatal or lead to serious conditions, such as graft vs. host disease. Orca Bio is a commercial-stage biotechnology company redefining the transplant process by developing next-generation cell therapies with the goal of providing significantly better survival rates with dramatically fewer risks.With our purified, high-precision cell therapies we hope to not only replace patients' blood and immune systems with healthy ones, but also restore their lives.
Position Summary: Reporting to our Chief Development Officer, the Director/Head of Pharmacovigilance will lead and develop the safety function, providing direct guidance to a small, dedicated team while driving end-to-end operational oversight.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead risk management and mitigation activities for assigned products, leading safety data review and analysis for all products.
  • Responsible for providing safety-related content for all clinical and regulatory documents.
  • Lead inspection preparedness efforts for pharmacovigilance and represent Orca’s pharmacovigilance organization at regulatory inspections.
  • Stay abreast of changes in regulations, leading updates to SOPs and other documentation to address any process gaps.
  • Identify and address resource and infrastructure needs, contribute to departmental budgets and planning to align with Orca products’ stage of development.
  • Represent product safety in the cross-functional team environment.
  • Lead safety governance activities in collaboration with medical monitors and leadership.
  • Lead safety related activities for regulatory filings including development of meeting request and briefing book content, SAP and TFL review, signal detection and risk identification, responses to regulatory queries, RMPs, REMs, ISS strategy, and regional safety related labeling activities.
  • Provide guidance and mentorship to all direct reports within the pharmacovigilance function, including support and oversight of operations.

Qualifications

  • Advanced degree in a biologic/medical/clinical/nursing field: Pharmacist/PharmD, Nurse Practitioner, MD, or PhD.
  • 10+ years of experience in drug safety, safety science and risk management at a pharmaceutical, biotech, or CRO, including people leadership experience.
  • Knowledge of US and EU safety regulations pre and post marketing pharmacovigilance requirements.
  • Experience with pharmacovigilance risk management, preferably at a commercial-stage company.
  • Proficiency in preparing pre-marketing and post marketing safety regulatory documents, including PSURs, PBRERs, PADER, and Risk Management Plans.
  • Experience with clinical development, risk/benefit analysis, and safety assessment.
  • Strong clinical, analytical, problem-solving, scientific writing, and communication skills.
  • Prior experience working on a BLA/NDA. Prior experience leading risk management activities for a BLA/NDA preferred.
  • Hands-on mentality, ability to operate in a small biotech environment.
  • Knowledge of cell therapy, bone marrow transplant or hematology oncology is a plus.
  • Expertise in analyzing safety data from clinical and safety databases.
  • Experience in MedDRA coding and search strategies.
  • Excellent independent judgment based on knowledge and expertise.
  • Strong personal time management and project management skills.
The anticipated annual salary range (listed above) for this job is based on prior experience in the role/industry, education, location, internal equity, and other job-related factors as permitted by law. For remote-based positions, this range may vary based on your local market. Full-time employment positions will also be eligible to receive pre-IPO equity and annual bonus, in addition to competitive medical, dental, and vision benefits, PTO, 401(k) plan, life and accidental death and disability coverage, and parental leave benefits. Other perks include subsidized daily lunches and snacks at our on-site locations.

Who we are

We are driven by a passion for science and compassion for patients. We act with urgency to ensure our treatments are one day accessible to all who need them.
We live by our core values of passion, courage, and integrity. Excellence in our work means the chance to unlock a better quality of life for our patients, and with that comes tremendous responsibility.
We innovate on a path that hasn’t been paved. We embrace an entrepreneurial spirit and take calculated risks to achieve our mission. We aren’t afraid to ask “why not” and challenge the status quo.
We maintain a start-up culture of camaraderie and leadership by example, regardless of title.
We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and recognize that celebrating our differences creates stronger, lasting solutions that better serve our team, our patients and their healthcare providers.

Notice to staffing firms

Orca Bio does not accept resumes from staffing agencies with which we do not have a written agreement and specific engagement for a particular opening. Our employment activities, inquiries and offers are managed through our HR/Talent team, and all candidates are presented through this channel only. We do not accept unsolicited resumes, and we rarely outsource recruitment.

raw.description:
Arbol is a global climate risk coverage platform and FinTech company offering full-service solutions for any business looking to analyze and mitigate exposure to climate risk. Arbol’s products offer parametric coverage which pays out based on objective data triggers rather than subjective assessment of loss. Arbol’s key differentiator versus traditional InsurTech or climate analytics platforms is the complete ecosystem it has built to address climate risk. This ecosystem includes a massive climate data infrastructure, scalable product development, automated, instant pricing using an artificial intelligence underwriter, blockchain-powered operational efficiencies, and non-traditional risk capacity bringing capital from non-insurance sources. By combining all these factors, Arbol brings scale, transparency, and efficiency to parametric coverage.

We are looking for a highly capable Strategy & Operations Associate to help build and scale a growing fintech business.

You will work closely with senior leadership and collaborate across product, technology, sales, finance, and operations. The role combines analytical problem-solving with hands-on execution: you will identify important business problems, develop practical solutions, and remain involved until those solutions are working in practice.

This is not a purely advisory role. You will have direct ownership over critical workflows, operating metrics, and cross-functional initiatives that affect customers, partners, and financial performance.

The ideal candidate is a smart, adaptable generalist who learns quickly, exercises strong judgment, and enjoys bringing structure to ambiguous problems.

What You'll Be Doing

    • Own and improve critical business workflows across customer onboarding, transaction execution, account servicing, partner management, reporting, and other core operations
    • Identify operational bottlenecks and build scalable processes, controls, and documentation to address them
    • Work with product and engineering teams to translate business needs into clear requirements for internal tools, customer-facing products, and automation
    • Build reporting that gives the team visibility into growth, conversion, turnaround times, service levels, unit economics, and other key performance indicators
    • Analyze business performance and recommend changes to improve growth, efficiency, economics, and customer experience
    • Coordinate across product, technology, sales, finance, operations, and external partners to keep important initiatives moving
    • Support the development and launch of new products, partnerships, and distribution channels
    • Conduct market, competitor, and strategic analysis to inform business priorities
    • Manage high-priority projects from initial problem definition through implementation and ongoing performance monitoring
    • Help establish the operating cadence, processes, and infrastructure required to scale the business
    • Step into emerging problems that do not fit neatly within an existing function and take responsibility for resolving them

What You'll Need

    • One to two years of experience in management consulting, investment banking, startup operations, fintech, or another analytically rigorous environment
    • Management consulting experience is especially attractive because of the role’s emphasis on structured problem-solving, cross-functional execution, and working through ambiguity
    • Strong analytical skills and comfort working with financial and operational data
    • An ability to understand complex systems, identify what matters, and translate analysis into action
    • Strong project-management skills, including the ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders and drive work forward without constant supervision
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
    • High attention to detail without losing sight of broader commercial priorities
    • Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment where responsibilities may evolve as the business grows
    • A low-ego, high-ownership approach and a willingness to move between strategic analysis and detailed execution
    • Proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets; experience with SQL, data-visualization tools, workflow automation, or AI-enabled tools is helpful but not required

What's Great to Have

    Direct fintech or financial-services experience is helpful but not required. Intellectual curiosity, commercial judgment, and the ability to learn quickly are more important.

Candidates for this role must be located in the United States.

Essential Job Functions & Physical Requirements

  • Ability to sit for extended periods of time while working at a computer, with or without reasonable accommodation
  • Ability to use a computer, keyboard, mouse, and standard office equipment (e.g., phone, printer, scanner)

  • Ability to maintain focus and attention while performing detailed tasks

Arbol values the perspectives and experience of candidates with non-traditional backgrounds and we encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every requirement.

raw.description:
9th Way Insignia is a service-disabled, veteran-owned small business bringing transformative technology to our government customers so they can achieve their missions. Our specialties include cybersecurity, cloud modernization, software development, data analytics, enterprise architecture, enterprise IT, analytics, process automation, and artificial intelligence. Learn more about 9th Way Insignia at

Application password: Niner

Team (Project) Introduction

We are recruiting for a range of cybersecurity opportunities supporting federal customers, focused on strengthening enterprise security architecture, systems engineering, and the secure implementation of technologies across the environment.

The work involves applying established cybersecurity standards, guidelines, and frameworks to help translate organizational and business requirements into secure, scalable technical solutions. Team members may contribute to security architecture and engineering efforts, implementation guidance, technical analysis, and the development of repeatable approaches that support the consistent deployment and operation of secure technologies across complex enterprise environments.

Systems security engineering is an important component of this work, with an emphasis on incorporating security and stakeholder protection requirements throughout the system development life cycle, from concept and design through development, production, sustainment, and decommissioning. The team will apply established systems engineering and cybersecurity principles to help protect systems, applications, data, and supporting technologies.

Ultimately, this work supports the broader mission to strengthen its cybersecurity posture, reduce organizational risk, and protect critical systems and information from evolving cyber threats, including external adversaries and insider threats.

9th Way Insignia is looking for an Engineer, 3, Configuration Management and Documentation Specialist/Tech Writer to join this team.

Professional Level Information:
An Engineer, 3 typically plans and directs research or development work on complex projects, along with engaging various parties in design and development. Costs and recommendations of new components may also involve part of the job scope. Performs multiple engineering-related tasks in various assignments within the project and firm. An Engineer, 3 oversees the design, development, implementation, and analysis of technical products and systems. An Engineer, 3 has broad knowledge of engineering procedures and assists in the resolution of complex problems. An Engineer, 3 has strong technical skills and background, a knack for learning new technologies, and a blend of good problem-solving and innovation needed to resolve a wide variety of technical production challenges.

Functional Job (LCAT) Information:
The Configuration Management & Documentation Specialist/Tech Writer will provide technical documentation, configuration management, change management, and knowledge management support for the program. The specialist will work closely with cybersecurity architects, engineers, project managers, technical SMEs, and Government stakeholders to develop, maintain, control, organize, and publish accurate technical documentation throughout the system and project lifecycle.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop, edit, format, maintain, and publish technical documentation supporting cybersecurity architecture, security engineering, operations, modernization, and program management activities.
  • Translate complex technical concepts, engineering designs, cybersecurity requirements, and SME input into clear, concise, accurate, and audience-appropriate documentation.
  • Develop and maintain technical products such as standard operating procedures (SOPs), technical procedures, plans, reports, diagrams, templates, configuration documentation, training materials, test documentation, and other contract deliverables.
  • Review technical documents for clarity, consistency, accuracy, completeness, grammar, formatting, terminology, and compliance with Government-approved templates and standards.
  • Coordinate with cybersecurity architects, engineers, analysts, developers, project managers, and other technical SMEs to collect information and ensure documentation accurately reflects technical solutions, system configurations, risks, requirements, and operational processes.
  • Document technical processes, system configurations, operational procedures, change-management processes, and configuration-management procedures to establish an accurate and auditable technical record.
  • Support the development and maintenance of configuration-management and change-management processes for systems, applications, infrastructure, documentation, and technical deliverables.
  • Identify, establish, track, and maintain configuration items, including hardware, software, technical documentation, system components, baselines, and other controlled deliverables.
  • Maintain accurate records of configuration status, document revisions, approvals, ownership, dependencies, and changes throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Support the establishment and maintenance of configuration baselines and ensure technical documentation remains synchronized with the current Government-approved system or engineering baseline.
  • Maintain and support a centralized Configuration Management Database (CMDB) or comparable configuration repository to ensure configuration information is current, accurate, traceable, and accessible to authorized stakeholders.
  • Apply IT Service Management (ITSM) and ITIL principles and practices to configuration, change, document, and lifecycle-management activities.
  • Establish and maintain an organized, searchable, and version-controlled Artifact Library that serves as the authoritative repository for contract-related documentation and technical artifacts.
  • Apply Government-approved taxonomy, naming conventions, metadata, document categorization, version control, and records-management practices to technical artifacts.
  • Ensure plans, reports, diagrams, templates, SOPs, configuration documents, test evidence, technical deliverables, and other required artifacts are properly stored and maintained within the approved repository.
  • Maintain document histories and ensure artifacts clearly identify appropriate dates, versions, revisions, approvals, status, and configuration baseline information.
  • Ensure documentation reflects the most recent Government-approved baseline and coordinate updates when systems, requirements, processes, architectures, configurations, or technical solutions change.
  • Implement and maintain document-access controls so that only authorized personnel can add, modify, approve, or delete controlled artifacts.
  • Support timely submission, publication, and repository upload of all contractually required technical deliverables.
  • Perform quality-control reviews of deliverables prior to Government submission to verify compliance with formatting, template, content, accessibility, and documentation requirements.
  • Ensure documentation complies with applicable Section 508 accessibility requirements and Government-approved templates.
  • Support development and maintenance of Security Architecture, Security Engineering, and Cybersecurity Operations documentation, including assessment reports, risk analyses, architecture artifacts, configuration baselines, technical recommendations, and implementation guidance.
  • Develop and maintain technical configuration documentation describing system or workflow configurations, setup parameters, routing logic, interfaces, integration points, architectures, and operational procedures.
  • Develop stakeholder training guides and user documentation providing clear, step-by-step instructions for technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Develop or support preparation of meeting minutes, technical briefing materials, status reports, information papers, recommendation reports, and executive-level presentations.
  • Support development and maintenance of technical diagrams, data-flow descriptions, architecture documentation, network topology information, process flows, and system configuration descriptions.
  • Maintain traceability between technical requirements, configuration items, engineering changes, documentation updates, and approved system baselines.
  • Support formal change-control activities, including documenting proposed changes, tracking approval status, updating affected documentation, maintaining revision history, and verifying implementation records.
  • Participate in configuration-control, technical-review, engineering, and project meetings and document decisions, actions, technical changes, risks, and required documentation updates.
  • Coordinate document reviews and approval workflows among Government stakeholders, project leadership, cybersecurity SMEs, and engineering teams.
  • Monitor documentation status and identify missing, outdated, inconsistent, or noncompliant artifacts, coordinating corrective updates with responsible technical personnel.
  • Support knowledge management and knowledge transfer by ensuring technical information is organized, accessible, current, and sufficiently documented for continued operations and future personnel.
  • Develop and maintain documentation necessary to support transition activities, including policies, procedures, SOPs, baseline information, metrics, technical documentation, and knowledge-transfer materials.
  • Protect sensitive information contained in technical documentation and ensure documents are stored, transmitted, and accessed using approved Government security controls and procedures.
  • Maintain documentation throughout the full project lifecycle, from initial development and engineering through implementation, operations, maintenance, modernization, transition, and decommissioning.
  • May require up to two onsite travel visits per year

Requirements:

  • Minimum of 5 years IT experience of which at least 3 years are of Configuration Management/Tech Editing experience at a large corporation or Government agency similar in size/scope to GSA, IRS, DoD or VA.
  • A Master’s degree in a related IT field (i.e. Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Systems, Information Assurance, Information Security, Information Resource Management).may substitute for up to 2 years of the required experience
  • Expertise configuration management, change management, or related roles within IT or software development environments.
  • Expertise overseeing and maintaining configuration items such as hardware, software, documentation, and other deliverables.
  • Expertise with documenting technical processes, system configurations, and change management procedures to ensure an accurate record.
  • Expertise with IT service management (ITSM) frameworks and best practices (e.g., ITIL). Proven experience in maintaining a centralized. configuration management database (CMDB).
  • Expertise in project management or working in a project-oriented environment, with an understanding of how configuration management fits into the overall project lifecycle within a large corporation and Government agency similar in size/scope to GSA, IRS, DoD or VA.
Preferred/Desired:
  • Bachelor’s degree or Associates degree in IT related field (i.e. Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Systems, Information Assurance, Information Security, Information Resource Management).
  • CASP+ (SecurityX), CCISO, CISA, CISM, CISSP, CISSP-ISSAP, CISSP-ISSEP, GCED, GCIH, GSLC, CCNP Security

raw.description:
About Midnight

Midnight is building a regulatory-friendly data protection blockchain designed to safeguard sensitive commercial and personal data while enabling developers, enterprises, institutions, and ecosystem partners to build privacy-preserving applications.

The Midnight Solutions team works with partners, developers, Product, Engineering, Developer Relations, Business Development, Growth, and Marketing to help turn real use cases into successful adoption of Midnight technology.

Role Summary

The AI Developer Tools Engineer makes Midnight a first-class target for AI-assisted and agentic software development. This role owns the tooling that lets AI coding agents build on Midnight, maintains Midnight Expert and the Foundation's other AI-enabled developer tools, and turns real usage feedback from builders and agentic tooling into concrete input for the core protocol roadmap. The role works closely with, and reports to, the Head of Product, and sits at the intersection of developer experience, protocol strategy, and applied AI tooling.

  • Makes Midnight buildable by AI coding agents, not just human developers, by shaping the tooling, context, and documentation those agents rely on
  • Owns the day-to-day maintenance and quality bar of Midnight Expert and other AI-enabled dev tools used by the community
  • Acts as the listening post for how agentic tooling and builders actually use Midnight, and translates that into structured input for the protocol roadmap

Core Responsibilities

Enabling Agentic Development on Midnight

  • Own and improve the tooling, context files, SDKs, and documentation that let AI coding agents (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot-style agents) build on Midnight effectively
  • Design, build, and optimize agent harnesses and orchestration workflows for Midnight-specific development tasks
  • Identify and close gaps where agentic tooling fails, hallucinates, or produces incorrect Midnight-specific code
  • Build and maintain reference implementations, prompts, and examples that improve agent output quality
  • Evaluate new agentic coding tools and protocols (e.g. MCP servers) for relevance to the Midnight developer ecosystem

Builder & Agentic Tooling Feedback Loop

  • Monitor how builders and agentic tools are actually using Midnight — successes, failure modes, and workarounds
  • Synthesize feedback from agentic tooling usage and community builders into clear, structured input for the core protocol roadmap
  • Maintain a regular reporting cadence to Product and Engineering on developer/agent experience trends and blockers
  • Represent the AI-assisted builder perspective in roadmap and prioritization discussions

AI Dev Tooling Maintenance

  • Own ongoing maintenance, accuracy, and reliability of Midnight Expert and other AI-enabled developer tools for the community
  • Keep tool knowledge bases, embeddings, and reference content current as the protocol evolves
  • Triage and resolve community-reported issues with AI dev tooling
  • Define and track quality metrics (accuracy, usefulness, adoption) for AI-enabled dev tools

At DYOPATH, we partner with private equity firms and their portfolio companies to transform technology into a competitive advantage. Through technology advisory, managed services, cybersecurity, cloud modernization, and M&A support, we help investors and executive teams improve operational performance, reduce risk, and maximize enterprise value.

Why DYOPATH?

As our Private Equity & M&A Practice continues to grow, we are seeking a Senior Solutions Architect, Private Equity & M&A, to serve as a trusted advisor to private equity sponsors, operating partners, investment teams, and portfolio company leadership.

This is not a traditional solutions architecture role.

DYOPATH is one of the nation's leading managed service providers and technology consulting organizations, helping businesses solve complex challenges through technology.

In this role, you'll have the opportunity to:

You will operate at the intersection of private equity, technology strategy, M&A, cybersecurity, managed services, and business transformation. Working directly with investors and executive leadership teams, you will help organizations assess technology risks, support acquisitions and integrations, improve operational effectiveness, and implement strategies that drive measurable business outcomes.

The ideal candidate combines executive presence, business acumen, technical expertise, and a passion for helping organizations leverage technology to drive value creation.

Why This Role Is Unique

Technology has become a critical lever for value creation within private equity. Investors increasingly rely on technology partners to support due diligence, accelerate growth initiatives, reduce operating risk, improve scalability, and maximize investment returns.

As a Senior Solutions Architect within DYOPATH's Private Equity & M&A Practice, you will work directly with private equity sponsors, operating partners, portfolio company executives, and technology leaders to identify opportunities where technology can create measurable business impact.

Practice Development

What We're Looking For

raw.title: 2029 Fintech Academy - Greenwood Project Scholar Program
raw.excerpt: About The Greenwood ProjectAt Greenwood Project, we open doors in financial services for undergraduate freshmen.
raw.description:
About The Greenwood Project
At Greenwood Project, we open doors in financial services for undergraduate freshmen. We give our scholars three things: social capital, the network that comes from knowing people inside the industry. Academic and technical capital, the training the work actually requires. And aspirational capital, the belief that the seat belongs to you.
This is not a workshop series. Scholars commit to twelve months of training, deliver real work on real deadlines, and finish knowing whether this industry is for them. Many go on to internships and full time offers at our partner firms. All of them leave with a network they did not have before.
The Fintech Academy
This academy trains the analytical and operational foundation underneath financial services: how markets are structured, how money actually moves through systems, where it breaks, and what the rules require. Financial services now hires analysts, operators, and risk professionals in the same numbers it hires traditional finance roles, and those jobs are open to people who did not start out in finance.
Where this training leads
These are the roles this academy prepares you for, and they hire sophomores and juniors in real numbers. Each one maps directly to what you will study.
• Fintech product and operations analysis. Working alongside product and operations teams to find what is broken, decide what matters most, and make the case for fixing it. This is the role our capstone puts you in.
•Trading operations. Everything that has to happen after a trade is agreed. Confirming it, clearing and settling it, making sure the right money and securities land in the right accounts, and finding the break when they do not. Trading desks cannot function without this, and it is one of the largest entry points into a firm.
• Operations more broadly. The rest of the machinery: onboarding clients, moving payments, reconciling accounts, handling corporate actions. When operations fails, it is expensive and public.
• Risk, compliance, and fraud. Figuring out what could go wrong, how likely it is, and how much it would cost. This includes fraud detection and the checks that confirm who a firm is doing business with.

Program Overview
We are recruiting 100 scholars into the Fintech Academy for the 2029 cohort. Across all three Greenwood academies we will select 325.
You are eligible if you are currently a freshman graduating in 2030. We call this the 2029 cohort because Summer 2029 is the internship you are working toward.
When What happens
  • October 2026 to June 2027: Rolling admissions. Decisions every month. November is the priority round.
  • July 2027: Academy begins.
  • July 2027 to June 2028: Twelve months of training, from the summer after freshman year through your sophomore year.
  • Fall 2028: Junior year internship recruiting season. Greenwood supports you through interviews.
  • Summer 2029: The goal: a 10 week internship with a partner firm, the summer after your junior year.
  • Spring 2030: You graduate.

How rolling admissions works
We review applications and make decisions every month from October 2026 through June 2027. You will hear back within 4 weeks of the round your application lands in. Seats fill as we go, so the earliest rounds have the most of them open. Apply early.
You get one application
You submit one application for this cohort. Not one per academy, and not one per round. Our Talent & Recruitment team may move you to a different academy than the one you selected if your answers point somewhere else, so you do not need to get that choice perfect.
Every application gets one of three outcomes:
  • Accepted. You are in.
  • Deferred. We want to see more before we decide, usually your next term of grades. Your application carries forward automatically and you do not need to submit anything new. You will hear from us about two weeks before the next round of decisions, and again every month until we decide. You will not sit in silence.
  • Declined. Final for this cycle. Because this program only admits freshmen, we cannot reconsider you in a later round.
Deferral is the reason you can apply in an early round without taking a risk. If we are not ready to decide, we hold your application. We will not turn you away for applying before your first semester was finished.
Deadlines in this process are real. Once you apply, we will ask you for things on a schedule: transcripts, forms, sometimes an interview time. If you miss those deadlines, your application is declined rather than delayed. We hold this line because the program itself runs on deadlines, and how you handle ours tells us how you will handle those.
Please read this carefully: Internship placements are not guaranteed. Greenwood trains you, advocates for you, and puts you in front of our partner firms. Those firms make their own hiring decisions. What we guarantee is the preparation, the network, and honest feedback. The offer is something you earn.

What You'll Study

No prior finance or technical experience is required. Real effort is. Each module below builds on the one before it, and you will be working with real deadlines throughout.
  • Basic Market Structure. OTC versus exchange systems, liquidity fundamentals, and the key elements of market structure. OTC means over the counter, where a trade happens directly between two parties instead of on a public exchange. Liquidity is how easily something can be bought or sold without moving its price.
  • Inside the FinTech Stack. [DESCRIPTION NEEDED. Awaiting context from team.]
  • Data-Driven Decision Making. Pre-trade, execution, and post-trade processes, including clearing, settlement, and reconciliation. This is the full life of a trade, from the decision to buy through to confirming that the money and the security actually changed hands.
  • Regulation & Risk. Fraud detection, KYC and AML, data privacy, and consumer protection. KYC means know your customer and AML means anti money laundering, the checks a firm runs to confirm who it is doing business with and where the money came from.
Capstone: AI-Powered Customer Insights Lab: Scholars act as members of a fintech product or operations team, analyzing mock customer feedback to identify pain points, prioritize issues, and present strategic recommendations to a simulated leadership audience.
Building AI Fluency
Fintech is where AI stopped being a pilot project. In a 2026 Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance survey, 21 percent of financial services firms already had AI agents running in production and 52 percent were piloting them. Agents are doing real work today in underwriting, fraud detection, compliance, and operations. That means two things for you. The entry level work that used to be manual is going away. And someone has to test, monitor, and be accountable for the systems doing it instead. That someone is who we are training you to be.
Hands on with real tools. You will not just learn concepts. You will build working skill with the software and AI tools used on the job. Each Greenwood academy trains a different technical toolset, chosen to match the roles that academy actually feeds, so what you build here is specific to the operations, risk, and product side of financial technology rather than a general overview.
The judgment we are after: knowing what should be automated, what should not, and who is responsible when an automated system gets it wrong. Firms are hiring for that question right now and struggling to fill the seats.

What We're Looking For - Ideal Degree Backgrounds

Your major does not decide which academy fits you. Your interest does. Plenty of freshmen have not declared yet, and some schools do not allow it until sophomore year. Neither works against you. Major titles also vary from school to school, so if yours is named differently but covers the same ground, it counts. Tell us what it is called where you are.
Fields of study that line up with this academy
  • Computer Science
  • Computer Engineering or Software Engineering
  • Engineering, any discipline
  • Information Systems, Management Information Systems, or Information Science
  • Data Science or Data Analytics
  • Mathematics or Statistics
  • Finance, Economics, or Business Analytics with a quantitative or technical focus
  • Operations, Supply Chain, or Industrial Engineering
  • Risk Management or Risk Management and Insurance, where your school offers it
  • Product and design adjacent fields, including Human Computer Interaction, Cognitive Science, or Design
If you have not declared a major yet
You can apply as undeclared. What we need to see is that you are seriously pointed toward operations, risk, product, or the technology side of financial services. Undeclared is not a weaker application. An undeclared student who can show us the following is stronger than a declared student who cannot:
  • Courses you have taken or registered for next term, such as intro programming, calculus, statistics, or information systems
  • Clubs and activities that back it up: a hackathon, a coding or robotics club, a data or analytics group, a product or startup club, or a technical campus job
  • Anything you have built or taught yourself, including a project, a script, an app, a dashboard, or a certificate
  • If product management is what you are after, anything where you decided what to build and had to defend the decision counts, including a club project, a small business, or an event you ran
  • A clear answer to why this academy and not the Investment Banking or Sales & Relationship Academy
If your major is not on this list
If you have taught yourself to code, or you are the person people come to when something breaks, apply and tell us about it. Self taught is not a disadvantage here. It is often the strongest signal we get.
Technical skills you will build
You are not expected to arrive with any of these. You are expected to want them.
  • Market structure literacy, meaning how exchanges and OTC markets work and how liquidity is provided
  • Trade lifecycle fluency, from pre-trade decisions through execution, clearing, settlement, and reconciliation
  • Data analysis and presenting numbers honestly, including making a chart that tells the truth
  • Product thinking, meaning writing a clear requirement, prioritizing what matters, and saying no to the rest
  • A working understanding of financial systems and the technology infrastructure underneath them
  • Analytical frameworks for risk assessment and operational efficiency
  • Structured problem solving, meaning breaking a vague problem into parts you can test
  • Excel and data manipulation, which you will use more than you expect
  • Regulatory literacy, including know your customer and anti money laundering checks, data privacy, and consumer protection
  • Working with AI tools and evaluating what they produce
Soft skills and characteristics
Greenwood selects scholars who show grit, resourcefulness, and intellectual curiosity, along with:
  • Strong analytical and logical reasoning
  • A systematic approach to problems, rather than guessing until something works
  • Attention to detail and a commitment to precision
  • The ability to explain something technical to someone who is not technical. This is the skill that gets people promoted.
  • A collaborative mindset, because this work is always cross functional
  • Adaptability, since the tools you learn this year will not be the tools you use in five years
  • A continuous improvement mindset, and the instinct to ask why a process works the way it does.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

What Makes a Strong Fintech Academy Candidate?

The strongest candidates take things apart to see how they work. You should be comfortable not knowing the answer, willing to sit with a problem longer than is comfortable, and interested in systems rather than only outcomes. You do not need a technical background. You do need to be willing to be new at something in front of other people, without quitting.
What this takes
  • Twelve months, from the summer after freshman year through your sophomore year, on top of a full course load.
  • Roughly 6 to 8 hours per week, with heavier weeks around project deadlines.
  • Technical work does not compress well. You cannot cram a project the night before and have it run.
  • Managing your class schedule around program commitments and staying organized without being chased.
Eligibility Requirements
  • Currently enrolled as a freshman (Class of 2030) at an accredited four year institution
  • Minimum 3.2 GPA for standard consideration
  • Students with a GPA between 3.0 and 3.19 may apply with a required personal essay
  • Students below a 3.0 GPA are not eligible for this cycle
  • Your high school transcript, submitted with your application
  • Your first semester or first quarter college transcript, submitted with your application or as soon as grades post if you apply in an early round
  • A demonstrated commitment to excellence, integrity, character, and collaboration
If your GPA falls between 3.0 and 3.19, the essay is not a formality. Tell us what the number does not capture, and be specific about what you changed.
If you apply in an early round before you have a college GPA, we review your high school record first and confirm eligibility once your first term transcript arrives

What You'll Gain

  • Work you can show, not just claim. You will finish the capstone with an analysis you built and can walk someone through in an interview.
  • AI capability most candidates do not have. Working with AI tools inside real operations and risk problems, plus the judgment to know when to override what they produce.
  • Range. These skills travel. Operations, risk, and product analysis exist at banks, exchanges, payments companies, asset managers, startups, and technology firms, and the foundation is the same in all of them. You do not have to know which one you want yet.
  • A real network. One on one coaching, a mentor in the industry, and access to professionals at our partner firms.
  • Proof you can learn hard things fast. That is what this year is really for, and what every future employer is trying to find out about you.

We’re looking for a Senior Frontend Developer to join our team for an initial 6 months project and help us build high-quality web applications used in real-world projects. You’ll work mainly with React and TypeScript, taking ownership of features from the initial idea through to production. You’ll also have the opportunity to work on some interesting challenges around 3D visualisation, interactive maps, and data-heavy applications.

What you’ll do

  • Build and maintain web applications using React and TypeScript.
  • Work closely with Product, Design, Backend, and other developers to turn requirements into solid technical solutions.
  • Help shape and improve our frontend architecture and development practices.
  • Make sure our applications are fast, responsive, accessible, and easy to maintain.
  • Work with UI libraries and design systems to create consistent user experiences.
  • Review code and share knowledge and best practices with the team.
  • Work on 3D visualisations and interactive experiences directly in the browser.
  • Develop features around interactive maps and geospatial data.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in Frontend Development.
  • Strong experience with React.
  • Strong knowledge of TypeScript and JavaScript.
  • Experience working on large or complex web applications.
  • Good understanding of frontend architecture, patterns, and best practices.
  • Experience integrating REST APIs and working with backend services.
  • Strong knowledge of HTML, CSS, responsive design, and browser behaviour.
  • Comfortable working with Git and modern development workflows.
  • Ability to work independently, make technical decisions, and take responsibility for your work.
  • Good communication skills and a collaborative mindset.
  • English Level: Fluent
  • All candidates must be based in Portugal or Brazil

Nice to have

  • Experience with Material UI or other UI/component libraries.
  • Experience with Tailwind CSS or similar frameworks.
  • Experience with Three.js, WebGL, or other technologies for building 3D experiences in the browser.
  • Experience with Mapbox, Leaflet, OpenLayers, or similar mapping technologies.
  • Experience building applications involving large amounts of data or complex visualisations.
  • Knowledge of frontend performance optimisation.
  • Experience with automated testing.
  • Experience working in an Agile/Scrum environment.

A little extra

We’re particularly interested in people who enjoy working on things beyond traditional frontend development. We have upcoming projects involving 3D visualisation in the browser, so experience with Three.js, WebGL, or similar technologies would be a big plus. We also work with applications where maps and geospatial data play an important role. Experience with mapping libraries such as Mapbox, Leaflet, or OpenLayers is therefore very welcome.

Most importantly, we’re looking for someone who enjoys solving problems, cares about the quality of what they build, and wants to have a real impact on the products they work on!

raw.description:
Location: This position may be performed remotely, but requires the flexibility and willingness to travel as needed.

The Opportunity

The Assistant Director, Regulatory Affairs, Advertising & Promotion will be the regulatory lead for advertising and promotional activities at Praxis, helping us communicate about our medicines with accuracy, integrity, and urgency as we work to bring high-impact treatments to patients with CNS disorders.

You will own the regulatory review and approval of promotional materials and partner closely with Commercial, Medical Affairs, Legal, Regulatory Strategy, and Regulatory Operations to build an efficient, rigorous, and scalable promotional review capability. This is a highly visible role for someone who brings strong regulatory judgment, communicates directly, and is comfortable making thoughtful decisions in a fast-moving environment.

Success in this role requires more than knowing the regulations. You will anticipate issues, challenge assumptions, find compliant paths forward, and help teams solve problems early rather than simply identifying risk at the end of the process. You will operate with significant autonomy and accountability while building trusted partnerships across Praxis.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Own Regulatory Affairs review and approval of advertising and promotional materials across channels, including HCP and DTC materials, digital and social media, sales aids, speaker materials, congress materials, and disease awareness campaigns.
  • Apply strong regulatory judgment to ensure promotional communications are accurate, appropriately balanced, consistent with approved labeling, and compliant with applicable FDA regulations and guidance while helping teams identify practical paths forward.
  • Partner early with Commercial, Medical Affairs, and Legal to shape campaigns and claims, provide clear and actionable guidance, and reduce unnecessary late-stage revisions or approval delays.
  • Own required FDA promotional submissions, including Form FDA 2253 filings, and lead Regulatory Affairs interactions with the FDA Office of Prescription Drug Promotion (OPDP), including responses to inquiries or enforcement communications.
  • Monitor OPDP enforcement activity, evolving FDA guidance, and regulatory trends; translate what matters into clear implications and recommendations for Praxis teams.
  • Build and continuously improve scalable advertising and promotion processes, including effective review practices, compliant records and archiving, coordination with Regulatory Operations, and use of systems such as Veeva PromoMats and RIM.
  • Serve as a trusted regulatory partner across Praxis, including partnering with Regulatory Strategy on product labeling, Medical Affairs on scientific exchange and medical education, and cross-functional teams on market access, pre-approval information exchange (PAIE), launch readiness, and other complex communications.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in a scientific, pharmacy, health-related, or relevant discipline; an advanced degree such as a PharmD, MS, PhD, MD, or JD is preferred.
  • 8+ years of pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical industry experience, including at least 5 years focused on regulatory advertising and promotion.
  • Deep, current knowledge of FDA requirements and guidance governing prescription drug advertising and promotion, with the judgment to apply those requirements effectively in situations where the answer may not be black and white.
  • Experience supporting product launches, including pre-approval promotional planning and PAIE activities, is strongly preferred; experience in CNS, neurology, or rare disease is also preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience with Form FDA 2253 submissions, OPDP interactions, and review of promotional materials across HCP, DTC, digital, social, and other channels.
  • A self-directed builder who takes ownership, moves with urgency, stays curious, and is comfortable making well-reasoned decisions with limited precedent; familiarity with Veeva PromoMats, RIM, or comparable systems is preferred.
  • The physical and mental requirements of our roles include but are not limited to regular use of a computer, devices or other office equipment, clear communication, and occasional movement. You'll need comfort with screen work, basic hand coordination, and focus. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.
Annualized Base Salary
$200,000—$221,000 USD

Compensation & BenefitsAt Praxis, we believe that taking care of our people (and their people) is important, so we provide a world class benefits package to help you thrive.  This includes 99% of the premium paid for medical, dental and vision plans. We also provide company-paid life insurance, AD&D, disability benefits, and voluntary plans to personalize your coverage. Thinking about the future?  We match dollar-for-dollar up to 6% on eligible 401(k) contributions and sweeten the deal with long-term stock incentives and ESPP.  We provide a discretionary quarterly bonus, an extremely flexible wellness benefit, generous PTO, paid holidays and company-wide shutdowns.  Not to mention, you'll also be joining a phenomenal crew of colleagues who are smart, engaged and inspiring.  We aim high, collaborate hard, and produce results.  Let’s achieve the impossible together!

Company Overview

Praxis Precision Medicines is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company translating genetic insights into the development of therapies for central nervous system disorders characterized by neuronal imbalance. At Praxis we share a common vision of reshaping the human condition into a more freeing and fulfilled existence by developing high impact medicines for patients and families affected by and living with complex brain disorders. Our core Values of Trust, Ownership, Curiosity and Results are foundational to every aspect of our business and are exemplified by each and every one of our team members.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion
Guided by our core values, at Praxis Precision Medicines, Inc. we continue to DARE FOR MORE® to advance, promote, and champion diversity, equity, and inclusion by encouraging individuals to bring their authentic selves and perspectives to work each day. We are an equal opportunity employer and committed to providing opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, religious creed, color, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, sexual orientation, disability, genetics, military service and veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

Attention: Job Scam Alert
Praxis has recently become aware of fraudulent job recruitment postings from individuals claiming to represent Praxis. These postings seek financial information in connection with fraudulent opportunities for employment. If you suspect any fraudulent activity or misrepresentation in connection with a Praxis job opportunity, please report it to

does not accept unsolicited submissions from recruitment agencies for open positions. We ask all recruitment agencies to refrain from contacting any Praxis employee regarding any position. All unsolicited resumes submitted by recruitment agencies to any Praxis employee in any form or method will be deemed to be the property of Praxis, and Praxis explicitly reserves the right to hire those candidate(s) without any financial obligation to the recruitment agency.

raw.excerpt: About AlphaPointAlphaPoint is the infrastructure platform behind digital asset businesses worldwide.
raw.description:
About AlphaPoint

AlphaPoint is the infrastructure platform behind digital asset businesses worldwide. Since 2013, we have powered exchanges, brokerages, banks, and fintechs across dozens of countries, giving them the trading, custody connectivity, tokenization, treasury, and settlement capabilities they need to operate in digital assets at institutional scale.

We are not a collection of products in a box. AlphaPoint is a single platform with many capabilities: one integration that lets a client offer trading, brokerage, treasury, and stablecoin workflows to their end users, connect to the liquidity venues, custodians, and banking partners of their choice, and expand into new use cases without re-platforming. Every super app needs a super platform underneath it. That is what we build.

About the Role

We are hiring a Sales Executive to open new markets for the AlphaPoint platform, with APEX (our trading and brokerage infrastructure) and APEX Treasury (our treasury and settlement layer) as the lead offerings. This is a new-business role. You will build your own pipeline, run complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles from first conversation to signature, and land accounts that grow with us as they add capabilities.

Our buyers fall into two groups. The first are firms launching a new exchange or brokerage and looking for the platform to build it on. The second, and larger, are firms that already have an established base of end users or assets and want to give those users access to digital assets: investment platforms and online brokers, asset managers and trading firms, private wealth and RIA platforms, fintechs adding crypto to an existing product, and the retirement channel, where brokers and IRA providers are bringing bitcoin ETFs and spot crypto to retirement accounts.

This is a builder role for someone with deep domain knowledge. You know how a broker-dealer, an asset manager, or a wealth platform actually works, what they need from a technology partner to launch digital assets, and who inside the building signs off on it. You can hold a first meeting with a CEO and a working session with a head of trading or a CTO in the same day, and you can teach a market what it should be asking for.

What You Will Do

  • Own new-business revenue for the AlphaPoint platform in your territory, selling APEX and APEX Treasury as an integrated platform rather than as standalone products, and consistently meet or exceed quota.
  • Build pipeline from scratch through your own network, targeted outbound, referral and partner channels, industry events, and content, with disciplined territory and account planning behind it.
  • Lead complex sales cycles with multiple stakeholders across business, product, technology, compliance, and legal, from discovery and solution design through commercial negotiation and contract close.
  • Develop and execute go-to-market plays for each target segment: investment platforms and brokers, asset managers and trading firms, private wealth, fintechs entering crypto, and retirement and IRA providers.
  • Act as a trusted advisor to prospects on how to structure a digital asset offering: which capabilities to launch first, how to integrate with existing systems and custodians, and how to stay within the regulatory perimeter in each market.
  • Partner with Solutions Engineers, Product, and Engineering to scope integrations and pilots, and bring structured market and client feedback back into the roadmap.
  • Work with Marketing on segment-specific campaigns, case studies, and events, and represent AlphaPoint at industry conferences and forums to build visibility and credibility in your markets.
  • Maintain an accurate, well-qualified pipeline and forecast in HubSpot, with clear next steps and close plans on every opportunity, and report weekly on pipeline health and progress to target.
  • Resourceful and hands-on: finds a way to move a deal forward regardless of the tools or processes in place, and helps build the playbooks the rest of the team will use.

What You Bring

  • 8+ years of B2B enterprise or institutional sales experience in capital markets technology, fintech, and digital asset infrastructure, with a track record of closing six-figure, multi-year contracts and consistently achieving quota.
  • Deep domain knowledge of at least two of our target segments: online brokerage and investment platforms, asset management and institutional trading, private wealth and RIA platforms, fintech, or the retirement and IRA channel. You understand how these firms are structured, how they make money, and how they buy technology.
  • Working knowledge of the digital asset ecosystem, including trading and execution, qualified custody, stablecoins and settlement, and the regulatory considerations that shape how regulated firms approach crypto.
  • Proven ability to build pipeline independently. You have opened new accounts and new segments before, not only worked inbound or an installed base.
  • An established network among decision-makers at financial institutions, brokers, wealth platforms, fintechs, or custodians, and a demonstrated ability to turn that network into qualified opportunities.
  • Technical fluency to engage credibly with CTOs, heads of trading, and product leaders on integration, APIs, and platform architecture, and to translate that into business outcomes for the C-suite.
  • Strong commercial and negotiation skills across complex, multi-stakeholder deal structures, including partner-dependent deals where a custodian or liquidity provider is part of the solution.
  • Experience navigating regulated environments and a commitment to the highest ethical and compliance standards.
  • A data-driven approach to managing your business: rigorous CRM hygiene, accurate forecasting, and comfort using analytics and AI tools to prioritize and work your territory.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication, with the presence to present to executive audiences and the clarity to write a proposal a CFO will read.

Preferred

  • Experience selling trading, custody, or market infrastructure technology to broker-dealers, asset managers, or wealth platforms (for example, OMS/EMS, execution, clearing, or custody connectivity).
  • Existing relationships with qualified custodians, ETF issuers or distributors, IRA and retirement-account providers, or crypto-native liquidity providers.
  • Experience in a venture-backed or growth-stage fintech where you helped define the sales motion rather than inherit it.
  • Familiarity with white-label and API-first platform models and the economics of platform partnerships.

How We Work

You will report to the VP of Sales and work closely with a small, senior commercial, product, and solutions team. We value people who are direct, curious about how our clients’ businesses actually run, and generous with what they learn. We move quickly, own our outcomes, and treat every client as a long-term partner rather than a transaction.

raw.description:
About Us

Sophos is a cybersecurity leader defending 600,000 organizations globally with an AI-driven platform and expert-led services. Sophos meets organizations wherever they are in their security maturity and grows with them to defeat cyberattacks. Its solutions combine machine learning, automation, and real-time threat intelligence with frontline human expertise from Sophos X-Ops to deliver advanced, 24/7 threat monitoring, detection, and response.
Sophos offers industry-leading managed detection and response (MDR) alongside a comprehensive portfolio of cybersecurity technologies — including endpoint, network, email, and cloud security, extended detection and response (XDR), identity threat detection and response (ITDR), and next-gen SIEM. Together with expert advisory services, these capabilities help organizations proactively reduce risk and respond faster, with the visibility and scalability needed to stay ahead of evolving threats.
Sophos goes to market with a global partner ecosystem, including Managed Service Providers (MSPs), Managed Security Service Providers (MSSPs), resellers and distributors, marketplace integrations, and cyber risk partners, giving organizations the flexibility to choose trusted relationships when securing their business. Sophos is headquartered in Oxford, U.K. More information is available at .

Role Summary

As Vice President, Total Rewards, you will lead the strategy, design, and delivery of Sophos's global total rewards programs. You will bring deep rewards expertise and use reliable data, responsible AI, and automation to improve decisions, the employee experience, and how we operate at scale.

What You Will Do

  • Set total rewards strategy: Own and evolve a global total rewards strategy that supports our business goals, keeps us competitive, and meets local requirements across our workforce.
  • Lead executive compensation: Oversee analysis and reviews of executive compensation programs and support the preparation of materials for the Board.
  • Guide equity programs: Partner with the equity team to manage equity programs and ensure they align with our broader compensation framework.
  • Design compensation programs: Lead the design, evaluation, and delivery of base pay, variable pay, equity, and recognition programs, with a clear focus on fairness and market competitiveness.
  • Shape global benefits: Lead the evaluation and management of health, wellness, retirement, and other benefit programs that meet the changing needs of our global workforce.
  • Improve technology and analytics: Advance total rewards technology, analytics, compensation review solutions, and workflow automation in close partnership with HR Operations and HR Systems leaders.
  • Build the team: Lead and develop a global Total Rewards team, strengthening capability across rewards, analytics, and responsible AI.
  • Partner across the business: Build strong working relationships across HR, Finance, Legal, and other teams so our programs reflect business priorities and financial considerations.

What You Will Bring

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in total rewards, compensation, and benefits, ideally in a complex, global technology company.
  • Strong knowledge of global compensation practices, regulatory requirements, and market trends. Experience with the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Germany, and India is preferred.
  • Hands-on experience managing equity programs, including experience in a private equity environment.
  • A strong track record of designing and delivering total rewards strategies that support business results.
  • The ability to turn strategy into action, manage competing priorities, improve how work gets done, and build constructive relationships across the business.
  • Strong leadership and communication skills, with the ability to engage different audiences, lead teams, and guide change across the organization.
  • The judgment to move comfortably between strategic leadership and hands-on work when needed.
In Canada , the base salary for this role ranges from $188,000 to $313,000. In addition to base salary, we offer additional compensation including bonus eligibility and a comprehensive benefits package.  A candidate’s specific pay within this range will depend on a variety of factors, including job-related skills, training, location, experience, relevant education, certifications, and other business and organizational needs. ​

We’re an early-stage startup seeking an experienced, creative, and AI-forward Marketing Manager to help grow and scale our marketing efforts. In this role, you’ll develop, test, and expand customer acquisition channels, with a strong emphasis on building scalable channels beyond paid advertising.

You’ll be responsible for identifying new growth opportunities, experimenting quickly, improving campaign performance, and helping our product reach far and wide. With our product-led growth strategy, you’ll collaborate across teams to fuel customer acquisition, improve engagement, and expand our customer base.

Responsibilities

  • Identify, onboard, evaluate, and optimize new marketing channels to drive significant lead volume within target customer acquisition costs.
  • Build and scale marketing channels from zero to meaningful reach, especially outside of paid channels.
  • Use AI tools heavily to improve marketing workflows, accelerate experimentation, generate creative concepts, and scale campaign execution.
  • Develop strong written content for ads, emails, landing pages, campaigns, and other marketing materials.
  • Build a library of creative concepts to communicate value to different buyer personas.
  • Improve middle-of-funnel conversion rates through messaging and tactics that optimize customer engagement and retention.

Qualifications

  • You have strong startup experience and are comfortable working in a fast-moving, resourceful environment.
  • You are a heavy user of AI tools and know how to apply them to grow, automate, and scale marketing efforts.
  • You have experience scaling a marketing channel from zero to significant reach, ideally beyond paid acquisition.
  • You love brainstorming new concepts, ad creatives, campaign ideas, and messaging.
  • You have experience acquiring small businesses and prosumer customers.
  • You understand how to assess campaign impact and estimate the effort needed to generate results.
  • You can manage multiple projects simultaneously and identify the fastest path to value.
  • You bring a full stack of marketing skills, from ideation to execution and analysis.
  • You have experience managing paid digital marketing campaigns.
  • You have excellent command of the English language and are a strong writer.
  • You’re able to create compelling content for ads, emails, landing pages, and campaigns.
  • You have a creative mindset and an eye for design, brand, and visual communication, and have used that ability to author copy, images, and videos with AI assistance.
